Ustyluh Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Volynska oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Jews are first mentioned in Ustyluh in the 17th century; the town became an important Hasidic center across the 18th and 19th centuries, famous for the 'Wedding at Ustila' in 1813, when some 200 Hasidic leaders gathered to debate whether the Pshiskha variant of Hasidism deviated from the broader movement. The Jewish population reached 3,212 (89 percent) by 1897, supported by 12 Hasidic synagogues. This cemetery, estimated to date to the 18th century, was the site of shootings in 1941 and 1942; following the 1942 ghetto's liquidation, 1,847 of Ustyluh's Jews were killed that September, and no Jewish community remained afterward.
